---
id: cpp-booking-calendar
title: Lab Booking Calendar
difficulty: Medium
order: 1
tags: std::map, lower_bound, intervals, ordered queries
time_limit: 2
---
## Statement
A robotics lab books its test arena in half-open intervals `[s, e)`. Process `q` commands online:

| Command | Effect | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `book S E` | book if it overlaps no existing booking (touching is fine) | `ok` or `conflict` |
| `cancel S` | cancel the booking that **starts** exactly at S | `ok` or `none` |
| `next T` | the earliest booking with start ≥ T | `S E` or `none` |
| `at T` | the booking containing time T (s ≤ T < e) | `S E` or `free` |
| `free_from T L` | the earliest time ≥ T at which a gap of length L begins | the start time |

q is up to 200 000 and times fit in `long long`, so every command must be O(log n) (except `free_from`, which may walk forward over bookings, but the tests keep that total reasonable). Store the bookings in a `std::map<long long, long long>` from start to end.

## Starter
```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <map>
#include <string>

int main() {
    std::ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(nullptr);
    int q;
    std::cin >> q;
    std::map<long long, long long> cal;
}
```

## Hints
- Overlap check for a new `[s, e)`: let `it = cal.lower_bound(s)`. There's a conflict if `it` exists and `it->first < e` (the next booking starts inside), or if `it` isn't `begin()` and `prev(it)->second > s` (the previous booking runs past `s`).
- `at T`: `it = cal.upper_bound(T)`. If it isn't `begin()`, step back one and check `T < it->second`.
- `free_from T L`: start with `t = T`. If a booking contains `t`, move `t` to its end. Then look at the next booking: if it starts at least `L` after `t`, answer `t`, otherwise move `t` to its end and repeat.

## Solution
```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <map>
#include <string>
#include <iterator>

int main() {
    std::ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(nullptr);
    int q;
    std::cin >> q;
    std::map<long long, long long> cal;               // start -> end

    auto containing = [&](long long t) {              // booking with s <= t < e, or end()
        auto it = cal.upper_bound(t);
        if (it == cal.begin()) return cal.end();
        --it;
        return t < it->second ? it : cal.end();
    };

    std::string cmd;
    while (q-- && std::cin >> cmd) {
        if (cmd == "book") {
            long long s, e;
            std::cin >> s >> e;
            auto it = cal.lower_bound(s);
            bool clash = (it != cal.end() && it->first < e) ||
                         (it != cal.begin() && std::prev(it)->second > s);
            if (clash) std::cout << "conflict\n";
            else { cal.emplace_hint(it, s, e); std::cout << "ok\n"; }
        } else if (cmd == "cancel") {
            long long s;
            std::cin >> s;
            std::cout << (cal.erase(s) ? "ok\n" : "none\n");
        } else if (cmd == "next") {
            long long t;
            std::cin >> t;
            auto it = cal.lower_bound(t);
            if (it == cal.end()) std::cout << "none\n";
            else std::cout << it->first << ' ' << it->second << '\n';
        } else if (cmd == "at") {
            long long t;
            std::cin >> t;
            auto it = containing(t);
            if (it == cal.end()) std::cout << "free\n";
            else std::cout << it->first << ' ' << it->second << '\n';
        } else if (cmd == "free_from") {
            long long t, len;
            std::cin >> t >> len;
            if (auto c = containing(t); c != cal.end()) t = c->second;
            for (auto it = cal.lower_bound(t); it != cal.end() && it->first - t < len; ++it)
                t = it->second;                       // bookings never overlap, so t only moves forward
            std::cout << t << '\n';
        }
    }
}
```

Because bookings never overlap, a `map` keyed by start time is a complete interval structure: neighbours in key order are neighbours in time. `lower_bound` and `upper_bound` find the relevant neighbours in O(log n), and the conflict test only needs to check the one booking before and the one after. `emplace_hint(it, ...)` inserts at the position already found, which is amortised O(1). `cal.erase(key)` returns the number of erased elements (0 or 1), conveniently answering "was there one?".
